ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC-compliant screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and individuals with significant control against Canada's Consolidated Federal Autonomous Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, and FINTRAC's Politically Exposed Persons database; application of risk-based enhanced due diligence, ongoing transaction monitoring, and mandatory report filing per the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC Guidance on politically exposed persons and sanctions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry, operated by Service Alberta, and the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system, accessible through authorized Alberta Registry Agents
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet using English or French renderings; non-Latin scripts require certified transliteration before filing; names must be distinguishable from existing registered names and must not be deceptively misdescriptive under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and Alberta Corporate Registry naming policy.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Audit or Auditor (where implying licensed public accounting)
Accountant or Accounting (subject to CPA Alberta regulatory consent)
Engineer or Engineering (subject to APEGA permit)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the Alberta Corporate Registry, the applicant or authorized registry agent may file a written reconsideration request with the Director of Corporate Registry within 30 days, attaching the original NUANS report, identification of any confusingly similar names, and supporting consents or undertakings; if refused, the applicant may pursue an administrative appeal and subsequently judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Administrative Procedures Act; concurrently, a fresh NUANS reservation may be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this ISIC 7020 ESG carbon advisory industry provided the registered office is a real physical street address in Alberta where service of process can be received; mail-forwarding-only and post-office-box addresses are prohibited; co-working and corporate agent office addresses constitute acceptable commercial substance for this Low_Risk_Standard non-licensed business classification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified annual inspection probability of approximately 5% for this low-risk, non-licensed advisory business; unannounced physical inspections are unlikely absent a regulatory complaint, but FINTRAC and applicable law enforcement authorities retain inspection powers over AML/CFT compliance records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 6, 12, 15, 101, 105, 123
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (CorpRegister online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) filed under s 12(1) ABCA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by the ABCA for incorporation; minimum_capital_requirement is false. Shares may be issued with no par value and there is no statutory escrow or paid-up capital holding requirement. 100% non-resident ownership is permitted under ABCA.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation subscribe for the shares issued upon incorporation; that the registered office of the Corporation be established at [address], Alberta; that [Director A] and [Director B] be and are hereby appointed as the first directors; that the following officers be appointed: [Name], Chief Executive Officer; [Name], Chief Financial Officer; and [Name], Corporate Secretary. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors be authorized to open a corporate bank account, to execute the corporate seal, and to file all necessary returns with the Alberta Corporate Registry and the Canada Revenue Agency. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers be authorized to execute all documents required to carry out the Corporation's business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (CorpRegister / authorized NUANS search houses)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) request to obtain a name search report. Verify that the proposed corporate name meets ABCA distinctiveness requirements and does not conflict with existing trademarks or corporate names. The NUANS report must be dated within 90 days of the subsequent incorporation filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the report identifies conflicting names, submit a revised name selection or obtain a written consent from the conflicting corporation to support the Name Reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Incorporation (Form 1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (CorpRegister online portal or paper filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute Form 1 stating the corporate name, full civic registered office address in Alberta, share structure (including classes, rights, restrictions and no-par-value provisions), proposed directors, and any restrictions on business. Pay the prescribed filing fee. Directors must sign consent to act in Form 1. Submit the application online for expedited processing or by mail for paper processing.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (valid within 90 days)
Directors' consent to act (included in Form 1)
Filing fee payment (CAD 275 online / CAD 300 paper)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for substantive defects, file corrected articles within 30 days of the deficiency notice; for minor errors, file Articles of Amendment (Form 4) after incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Post-Incorporation Tax Account Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta; Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which marks the commencement of the corporation's legal existence. Immediately thereafter, complete the CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) application to obtain a federal Business Number (BN), Alberta corporate tax account, and, if required, GST/HST and payroll accounts.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error, apply under s 207 ABCA for a correction certificate; federal and provincial tax account issues may be cured by filing an amended account request with the CRA or the Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Corporate Governance Formalities and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board of directors and corporate records office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board of directors meeting, adopt by-laws, confirm the registered office, appoint officers, allot and issue shares, and open a corporate bank account. Prepare the corporate records book containing the share register, director and officer registers, share certificates, and written consents.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board of directors meeting
Share certificate ledger and share subscription agreements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiencies in minutes or missing consents are cured by obtaining ratified resolutions executed by all directors and/or shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Occupational / Physical Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing department (e.g. City of Calgary Business Licence Program or City of Edmonton Corporate Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence for a professional office and consulting service. Confirm lease compliance with the Alberta Building Code, obtain fire safety inspection approval under the Alberta Fire Code, and register the mandatory workers' compensation coverage with WCB-Alberta.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement and building occupancy permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the premises are flagged for occupancy or fire safety defects, remediate with the landlord and municipal fire marshal; appeal licence refusal to the municipality's business licence appeal committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Optional Carbon Offset and ESG Regulatory Alignment (Alberta TIER / Voluntary Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (TIER Regulation); voluntary registries such as Verra or Gold Standard
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For Scope 1-3 carbon audit and offset brokerage services, register as a quantification advisor or project developer under the Alberta TIER program where clients seek compliance offsets; otherwise conduct voluntary carbon credit brokerage under contractual authority, supported by ISO 14064-3 validation and verification procedures. If the brokerage transmits client funds, register as a Money Services Business with FINTRAC.
required_dossiers: FINTRAC MSB registration (if funds remittance services are offered)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If TIER eligibility is questioned, submit a supplementary quantification and eligibility report for reassessment by the Alberta Environment and Protected Areas.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Ministry of Jobs, Economy and Trade (economic and commercial oversight); municipal licensing departments for local business registration; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas for carbon offset program alignment
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (General Professional Office / Management Consulting); no provincial industrial operating permit is mandated for NAICS 541620 environmental consulting services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Class B Professional Office use; EIA not triggered under the Environmental Assessment (Mandatory and Exempted Activities) Regulation AR 113/1993
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharges; office wastewater routed to municipal sanitary sewer within municipal discharge bylaw limits; negligible VOC and particulate emissions; electronic waste managed under the Alberta Recycling Regulation AR 226/2006

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the local fire department under the Alberta Fire Code (NFC 2019 adoption); structural load and building occupancy clearance under the Alberta Building Code; workplace hazard assessment and OHS program registration under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (SA 2020, c O-2.2); WCB-Alberta workers' compensation account and first aid / emergency preparedness readiness

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); official portal: 'My Business Account' and 'Business Registration Online' at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html. Alberta corporate income tax is administered under the federal-provincial Tax Administration Agreement and filed through the federal T2 return, with the Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration as the provincial receiving authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Canadian-resident Business Corporation obtains its statutory 9-digit Business Number (BN) automatically through the integrated incorporation process (federal via Corporations Canada/'Business Registration Online' or Alberta via the Alberta Corporate Registry's Corporate Online service). Non-resident and extra-provincial entities must register manually: first complete extra-provincial registration under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, then file Form RC431 (Application to Register a Non-Resident Corporation) or Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) with CRA. The BN is the universal tax identification number for federal and provincial corporate tax; a GST/HST account (BN + 'RT' sub-account) is activated in the same CRA application session, and the BN must be quoted on all invoices, GST/HST returns, T2 corporate income tax filings, and customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Canadian Business Corporation is a separate, non-transparent taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act, taxed on worldwide net income at the federal level plus Alberta corporate income tax through the collection agreement. No flow-through or partnership attribution is available to the corporation, and Canada does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box pass-through election for Canadian-resident corporations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regime for domestic corporations. The statutory elections relevant to an ESG carbon-advisory corporation include: (i) the GST/HST closely-related corporation election (Excise Tax Act s. 156), which treats qualifying group supplies as taxable at the recipient's rate and can eliminate GST on internal services; (ii) GST/HST group registration (ETA s. 273) consolidating compliance for a corporate group; (iii) hybrid-mismatch arrangement de minimis elections (Income Tax Act s. 18.4(3)); (iv) partnership designation elections (ITA s. 96(3)) for any co-owned joint venture; and (v) non-resident branch-tax elections (ITA s. 219). Each election is made on a prescribed CRA form within the applicable deadline and none alters the entity-level classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST); Alberta is a non-participating province with no provincial sales tax, so only the 5% federal GST applies and there is no HST component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in total taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) made during the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters — worldwide supplies for a resident corporation and supplies made in Canada for non-residents. Exceeding the threshold makes GST/HST registration mandatory; voluntary registration is available to recover input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, API-based invoice authorization, or digital stamping mandate. E-invoicing is voluntary, and the federal government is exploring non-mandatory Peppol-based exchange standards. GST/HST compliance is enforced through periodic returns (GST/HST NETFILE or EDI, mandatory for larger registrants generally exceeding CAD 1 million in gross annual revenue) and the ETA s. 286 books-and-records obligation, which requires invoices, receipts, and export substantiation to be retained in Canada or made available electronically on CRA audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7(d), a supply of services (including corporate Scope 1-3 carbon footprint auditing, verification, and ESG advisory) is zero-rated at 0% GST when made to a non-resident recipient who is not registered for GST/HST, unless the service relates to real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada, or is otherwise supplied for consumption in Canada. Intangible personal property such as carbon credits and emissions allowances supplied to a non-resident for offshore consumption may also be zero-rated under the applicable Part V provisions, while an offset-brokerage element that qualifies as an exempt financial service under Schedule VI, Part VII is disregarded for GST. Substantiation requires contemporaneous proof of the recipient's non-resident status, non-registration at the supply date, and offshore consumption of the service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency B13A / CARM electronic export report) for any tangible deliverables; for pure cross-border services, the governing service contract, statement of work, and engagement letter with the non-resident client constitute the primary export record

Bill of Lading, airway waybill, or courier/carrier certificate evidencing physical export from Canada for shipped goods or deliverables; electronic delivery logs and server/IP transmission records for digitally delivered ESG audit reports
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank credit confirmation from a Canadian financial institution evidencing receipt of export consideration from the non-resident
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reverse zero-rated treatment on audit where the export documentation is incomplete or fails contemporaneous substantiation, reassessing at 5% GST with compound interest and disallowed input tax credits where applicable. A knowingly false or grossly negligent zero-rating claim triggers ETA s. 280 civil penalties of 25% of the evaded tax, and conviction under ETA s. 327 carries a fine of 50%-250% of the evaded tax and/or imprisonment up to two years. Parallel income-tax exposure exists under ITA s. 163(2) (50% gross-negligence penalty) and ITA s. 239 (fine of 50%-200% of the tax evaded and/or imprisonment up to five years). Canada imposes no statutory FX-repatriation deadline; the 180-day figure is a best-practice audit-control benchmark, and unrepatriated export proceeds remain taxable in Canadian Part I income regardless of repatriation date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating under the Bank of Canada Act; foreign exchange and cross-border financial transactions are additionally governed by the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), the Currency Act, and relevant regulations administered by FINTRAC and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible on both current and capital accounts. Canada has no exchange control system, does not restrict remittance of profits, dividends, or capital repatriation, and has accepted Article VIII obligations under the International Monetary Fund Articles of Agreement. Profit remittances from an Alberta business corporation are subject to Canadian non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (typically 25%, reduced under applicable tax treaties), but no exchange-control authorization is required. Administrative hurdles are limited to bank KYC/CDD, source-of-funds documentation, and tax compliance certificates where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no designated timeline within which export receipts must be repatriated. Exporters may hold foreign currency balances in Canadian or offshore accounts, convert such funds at commercial rates, or use them for trade settlement. Canadian reporting obligations apply under the PCMLTFA for cross-border electronic funds transfers exceeding CAD 10,000, and exporters must maintain books and records under the Income Tax Act and Excise Tax Act for tax and customs verification.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium viability as a primary treasury rail, but acceptable as a payment-services supplement. Canada does not charter standalone electronic money institutions (EMIs) or digital-only banks as deposit-takers without a banking licence under the Bank Act (Schedule I or Schedule II) or an Alberta credit union charter. Offshore EMIs such as Wise or Revolut cannot offer Canadian IBANs, CAD clearing through Lynx, or CDIC-insured deposit accounts. They may operate as Money Services Businesses registered with FINTRAC and provincial authorities, but they are not a substitute for a regulated Canadian operational account. For this ISIC 7020 carbon advisory entity, an EMI could be used for low-value FX conversions, but all escrow and accounted settlements must sit with a Canadian prudentially regulated bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated federal or provincial business corporation establishing a first Canadian bank account in Alberta, the bank will require physical presence or an equivalent enhanced due diligence interview for at least one director or authorized signatory. In practice, Tier 1 banks assess on a case-by-case basis: a remote opening with video-verified identity, notarized corporate attestation, and a Canadian registered agent or resident director may succeed, but many institutions mandate an in-person visit to an Alberta branch for the initial account activation. The Canada Business Corporations Act and Alberta Business Corporations Act do not impose a residency requirement for directors, but banking policy and FINTRAC CDD rules create a high likelihood that physical verification of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner and approving signatory will be required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity where shareholders are trustee-held, layered, or non-resident
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate extract, register of directors, register of shareholders, beneficial ownership attestation signed by each 25%+ ultimate owner, organizational chart, declaration of source of wealth and source of funds, and notarized corporate resolutions authorizing the account signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client jurisdiction risk or nexus to a high-risk/listed jurisdiction in carbon offset trade
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Geographical risk matrix, commercial rationale for counterparty selection, export/import permits if applicable, proof of licence status of counterparties, and a written anti-money laundering compliance policy covering sanctions screening and PEP identification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for capital injection or substantial advisory fees paid to the escrow account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements or reviewed internal accounts, bank references from the remitting institution, share subscription agreement, capital contribution resolution, loan agreements for shareholder loans, tax clearance certificates, and evidence of business pipeline for advisory invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status of directors, shareholders, or beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PEP questionnaire, sworn declarations from all beneficial owners, passport copies, professional reference letters, and a written explanation of the business relationship with any foreign or domestic public official.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondent banking or transaction routing through opaque intermediary financial institutions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full wire routing map, SWIFT MT103/MT202 details, confirmation that no shell or unlicensed entities are in the chain, and an attestation that all intermediary financial institutions are regulated entities in their home jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or export-control exposure arising from cross-border carbon offset or ESG data services
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Global sanctions screening policy, proof of screening against OFAC, EU, UN, and Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions Lists, end-user declarations, carbon offset registry attestations proving the offsets originate from permissible jurisdictions, and legal opinions where a counterparty has nexus to sanctioned regions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from non-resident shareholders or parent companies should be routed through SWIFT MT103 (with MT202 cover if using an intermediary bank) to the Canadian bank's correspondent account, using the beneficiary's corporate operational account. The remittance must include a clear payment reference such as 'Capital Contribution' or 'Loan Disbursement' and reference the underlying share subscription or loan agreement. Canadian banks will require proof of source of funds, a completed corporate resolution, and tax information under the Canada-U.S. Intergovernmental Agreement or FATCA where applicable. There is no official Canadian 'purpose code' regime; instead, the bank will require a narrative purpose and may file a Large Cash Transaction Report or International Electronic Funds Transfer Report with FINTRAC if the transfer exceeds prescribed thresholds. For inbound capital exceeding the Investment Canada Act financial threshold, an application or notification under the Act may trigger, but this does not alter banking routing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for ESG carbon advisory and offset brokerage should settle primarily through international wire transfer using SWIFT MT103, or through commercial letters of credit for high-value offset purchases requiring payment against presentation of registry certificates. For CAD domestic settlements, the Lynx system (Canada's high-value payment system) provides final real-time settlement through chartered banks. US-dollar settlements can use correspondent accounts; cross-currency payments require clear SWIFT instructions SEPA or Fedwire. All outbound wires should include mandatory reference to the underlying invoice or offset registry serial number. For commercial LCs, the advising and confirming banks must comply with UCP 600. In all cases, the corporate entity is subject to FINTRAC reporting on outgoing EFTs over CAD 10,000 and to Canadian sanctions screening obligations under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Foreign exchange forwards (deliverable CAD/USD and CAD/EUR across standard tenors)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where a counterparty cannot physically settle CAD, although the Canadian dollar is freely deliverable and NDF is generally unnecessary
Cross-currency swaps between CAD and foreign currencies for treasury liquidity management
FX options and collars marketed by Canadian Schedule I banks or regulated broker-dealers for cash-flow hedging of advisory fee receipts and offset brokerage payables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two (2) months after the incorporation anniversary date; filed annually based on statutory anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Continuous failure to file for one year can trigger administrative dissolution and prevents issuance of certificate of compliance; no monetary late fee is assessed, but registry standing is downgraded to 'Inactive'.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six (6) months after fiscal year-end; instalment payments due on a quarterly basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (max 12 months); repeat non-filing raises penalty to 10% plus 2% per month; CRA daily prescribed interest applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Corporate Income Tax Return and Allocations (AT1-style through CRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA) via the CRA Tax Collection Agreement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal-year-end plus six (6) months, mirroring federal T2 due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Alberta may issue a non-filing estimate on income, add prescribed interest, and pursue collection through the Alberta Ministry of Treasury Board and Finance; habitual default can also impair registry compliance status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registered office, directors, and records custody
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records side; no separate filing unless underlying changes occur
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annotate minutes/register promptly and at each fiscal year-end review; annual-director resolution confirming registers is advisable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under ABCA directors may be personally liable for loss; records default exposes the company to valid oppression remedies and inspection orders by members and creditors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: ABCA does not impose a revenue-sized audit threshold. An independent auditor is required unless all shareholders waive the registrar requirement by unanimous resolution. Mandatory audited financial statements arise for distributing public corporations, regulated entities, or by shareholder demand requiring audited accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Publicly accountable corporations use IFRS under CPA Canada Part 1; private non-listed companies may use Canadian ASPE (Part 2) or choose IFRS consistently. ESG carbon-advisory revenue is normal operating revenue under IAS 1 / ASPE 3400.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta ABCA does not require annual public UBO filing; the annual return confirms directors and registered office. If incorporated federally under CBCA, the Individual with Significant Control register is internal, must be updated within 15 days of any prescribed change, and is subject to regulator inspection. At annual shareholder review, officers should verify share register accuracy and sign director minutes reflecting transfers.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,500 - $12,000 for a dormant-to-mid-size operating private corporation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sectoral tax holiday. General incentives: SR&ED ITC (non-refundable 15%, or 35% refundable for qualifying CCPCs), Alberta provincial tax rate already net of no capital levy. No preferential rate for ISIC 7020 ESG consulting.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically via CRA 'File T2 Online' through My Business Account or CRA-certified software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, based on the corporation's fiscal period (typically 12 months; first period may be up to 24 months)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the end of the taxation year (e.g., December 31 year-end due June 30 of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross fees from carbon footprint auditing, ESG advisory services, and offset brokerage commissions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation, report only revenue attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment (PE); worldwide income is otherwise reported only for the PE under Part I of the Income Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: salaries, subcontractor costs, professional fees, software subscriptions, travel, rent, and administrative overhead
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses reasonably allocable to the Canadian PE; head-office recharges must meet the arm's length standard under section 247.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after applying all deductions, tax adjustments, and available loss carryforwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute taxable income strictly from Canadian PE activities; any transfer pricing adjustments must be reflected before arriving at this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base federal tax calculated at 15% on taxable income (before credits and provincial allocation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply any applicable treaty rate relief only at the withholding stage; the federal tax cannot be reduced unilaterally by treaty in the T2 computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim only statutory credits such as SR&ED ITC that are available and otherwise unused in the year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents generally cannot claim credits unless the credit is specifically attributable to the Canadian PE and the taxpayer is eligible under the relevant provision.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; thereafter, minimum penalty for repeat offenders. Late or inadequate remittance: arrears interest compounded daily at CRA prescribed rate. False statements or omissions: 50% gross negligence penalty under s.163(2).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Alberta: AT1 Corporation Tax Return, filed separately with the Alberta Ministry of Treasury Board and Finance via Alberta Tax Access Portal (TAP) or authorized software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligning with the federal T2 filing period
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be filed by the same deadline as the T2: six months after the end of the taxation year (e.g., December 31 year-end due June 30)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income allocated to Alberta using the federal income allocation rules (e.g., permanent establishment, sales, payroll)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident with a PE in Alberta, report only the income attributable to that PE; the amount must match the federal allocated amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim any Alberta-specific credits, but none are available for ISIC 7020 carbon audit services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are generally not entitled to provincial credits unless the credit is specifically conferred.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Not applicable, Alberta does not levy corporate capital tax

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Penalty of 5% of unpaid Alberta tax, plus 1% per month up to 12 months, with an additional 5% penalty if the return is filed more than 6 months late. Interest on arrears accrues at the province's prescribed rate. Criminal prosecution for wilful evasion under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act applies to false filings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must complete and deliver CRA Form NR302 or NR303 (Certificate of Residency) to the Canadian paying corporation prior to the dividend payment. The payer then withholds at the reduced treaty rate (e.g., 5% for a US corporation holding at least 10% voting stock; 15% otherwise). If excess tax is withheld, the non-resident may file a T2 income tax return or a T1 individual return, as applicable, within two years of the end of the calendar year to obtain a refund. The Canadian payer must file Form NR301 (Statement of Entitlement) if relying on a treaty claim, and keep all supporting documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%; treaty rates usually 10% (0% for certain literary/artistic royalties, and 0% for certain software copyright payments under the Canada-USA treaty). Interest: statutory 25%; treaty rates typically 10% for arm's-length interest, 15% for non-arm's-length; 0% for interest on certain government export-finance obligations. For carbon-accounting proprietary software or methodology licenses, the reduced treaty rate is generally 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory when aggregate covered cross‑border transactions with non‑resident related parties exceed CAD 5 million in a taxation year; Master File required when such transactions exceed CAD 10 million. A T106 (Information Return) must be filed for any non‑arm's‑length cross‑border transaction where the aggregate value is over CAD 1 million (for loans/advances) or CAD 5 million (for other types of transactions).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations statute like the UAE. Instead, the CRA applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under section 245, the 'business purpose' test, and the OECD Multilateral Instrument’s Principal Purpose Test (PPT) to disregard shell arrangements and deny treaty benefits. For an ESG carbon advisory corporation, the CRA will scrutinize the existence of a real economic presence in Canada—such as actual office space, salaried employees, board decisions, and operational risk—before accepting claimed income allocation or treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission or false statement in the T2/AT1 such as understating audit revenue from offshore clients, fabricating carbon offset transactions, or claiming fictitious expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: On summary conviction: fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and/or imprisonment for up to 2 years. On indictment: fine up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years. Civilly, a 50% gross negligence penalty under s.163(2) applies, plus compound interest on the entire underestimation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who directed, authorized, or acquiesced in the act are jointly and severally liable for penalties under s.323, and may face criminal prosecution under s.242, including imprisonment, travel bans, and loss of capacity to act as a director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Documentation Violation (Income Tax Act, s.247)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare contemporaneous Master/Local File documentation when thresholds are exceeded, or setting intercompany charges for carbon advisory services or software royalties at non-arm's-length amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reassess taxable income to an arm's-length price, and a 10% penalty applies to the net upward adjustment if the taxpayer has not made 'reasonable efforts' to comply. Failure to provide documentation within 90 days of a formal request triggers a penalty of CAD 1,000 per month for each person (up to CAD 5,000).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participated in the mispricing may be assessed directly for the penalty and interest if they are found to be co-conspirators in a tax evasion scheme; in criminal cases, imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Shopping (GAAR and MLI PPT)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a Canadian shell corporation with no operational substance to route ESG consultancy fees from a treaty country to a third low-tax jurisdiction, or using a Canadian conduit to obtain a reduced treaty rate on dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA may apply GAAR to re-characterize the arrangement, deny treaty benefits, and impose the 25% statutory withholding tax retroactively. A 50% GAAR penalty under s.245(3.1) may apply if the arrangement is considered 'abusive'. Interest accrues from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who were aware of and endorsed the conduit structure may be jointly liable for the GAAR penalty, and in egregious cases, personal criminal exposure for money laundering or tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to implement a compliance program, or failing to report the receipt of funds exceeding CAD 10,000 from offshore buyers of carbon offsets through wire transfers that present suspected money-laundering indicators.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: up to CAD 500,000 for a first violation per assessment, and up to CAD 1,000,000 for subsequent violations. Criminal prosecution under s.90 of the PCMLTFA for deliberate non-compliance can lead to imprisonment for up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly aided or failed to take reasonable steps to report while having knowledge are liable for fines and imprisonment; additionally, the CRA may file a director's liability assessment for any unpaid corporate penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Remittance Failure (Part XIII and s.227.1)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold the statutory 25% (or applicable treaty rate) on dividends, interest, or royalties paid to non-residents, or failure to remit payroll source deductions to the CRA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A penalty of 10% of the amount not remitted, plus a 20% penalty for a second or later failure within a single year. The CRA may assess the full amount directly against the corporation, plus daily compounding interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally and jointly liable under s.227.1 for the entire unremitted amount, interest, and penalties, regardless of corporate dissolution; they can be pursued civilly, subject to a due-diligence defence, and restrictive travel or asset-freezing orders may be issued.
